decisions.reason: Resolves the omitted speaker as ‘his cold voice,’ which reads more naturally after Mukyung’s line without changing meaning.
Keeps the Korean’s comma-linked death list and ‘degree and form’ for 크기나 형태; SOL’s periods and ‘nature’ drift.
‘Took its place’ covers 빈자리를 채운; SOL’s ‘rushed in’ adds unsupported urgency.
One-sentence rise, swallow, and glare follows the 고 connective more cleanly than BASE’s split.
‘This fucking lunatic’ matches 이런 미친 새끼 as a jab at the man in front of him.
Keeps 당장이라도 as ‘right away’ and the punchy ‘Not because… Because…’ split; SOL drops the immediacy.
‘Immediately/as if’ and ‘at once/as though’ are interchangeable; no real gain.
‘Your days are numbered’ is the natural English for 명줄이 얼마 안 남았다.
Keeps the fragment after 반쪽짜리, ‘incomplete’ over ‘half-baked,’ and 놈 as ‘bastard.’
‘Both a Hunter and a martial artist’ is cleaner English for 인 동시에.
SOL’s ‘nothing but’ captures 단순한, but ‘but…either’ and ‘sheer luck’ warp the 고/것도 아니지 logic and 운이 좋아.
decisions.replacement: “Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi? First Rate master? Even a passing dog would laugh. You’re nothing but a brawler. You’re sloppy for a martial artist, and you don’t even fight as pragmatically as a wandering martial artist. Don’t mistake surviving through good luck for skill.”

decisions.reason: Preserves the physical 입을 열었다; SOL’s ‘speak’ erases that action.
Fronting ‘According to you’ matches 네 말대로면; ‘just luck’ is natural English for 그것도 운인가.
‘Idiot who let his guard down’ and ‘turn the tables’ are tighter renderings of 멍청한 놈 and 상황을 뒤집다.
Uses the project ellipsis character instead of a doubled Korean-style pause.
직접 보지도 않았으면서 is not seeing it, not being absent; SOL’s ‘wasn’t there’ over-specifies.
Keeps the rhetorical 몰랐을까 about Jopil and the 도 in 놈도; SOL adds ‘do you think’ and drops ‘too.’
새끼 is ‘bastard,’ not BASE’s softened ‘guy.’
‘Ends here’ is punchier spoken English for 여기까지야 without losing the cutoff.
Same ellipsis convention as H015.
방심하지 않아 is habitual ‘don’t,’ not SOL’s predictive ‘won’t.’
Keeps 폐부를 찌른다 as stabbing the vitals; SOL’s ‘struck deep’ flattens the image.
딱 여기까지 is ‘exactly this far’; SOL’s ‘as far as it could’ adds a capability claim.
하지만 is ‘But,’ not ‘Still.’
Keeps 풀이 as ‘solve’; SOL’s ‘fix’ and extra ‘ready to’ change the problem-solution joke.
Keeps glossary Murim and wandering martial artist, and 마시는 as drinking, not holding the cup.
Preserves 사람이 됐다 as becoming a decent human, distinct from 성장했다; SOL collapses both into growing up.
‘Pin down’ is the idiom for 종잡을 수가 없다, and ‘would work’ fits the general truth better than past ‘worked.’
하지만 is ‘But’; ‘Still’ is mere synonym churn.
‘None could match’ sets the prodigies contrast more naturally than ‘was unmatched.’
‘And’ carries 도, and ‘strengths’ matches the earlier 장점/단점 pairing.
Need both 눈 and 귀; BASE drops the body-part pair, SOL keeps the eye but replaces the ear with ‘good sense.’
decisions.replacement: He had the eye to grasp martial arts at a glance, excellent instincts in real combat, and an ear for other people’s advice.

decisions.reason: 비록…지만 is a factual ‘though,’ not SOL’s hypothetical ‘even if.’
‘Given time’ matches the 다면 conditional better than ‘As time passed.’
조화를 이룬 is taiji achieving harmony, not being ‘brought into’ it.
부담이 되다 is becoming burdensome; SOL’s ‘a lot of pressure’ adds degree and a ‘feel’ verb.
견딜 수가 없다 is stronger than ‘wondering,’ but SOL’s inserted ‘Jin Mukyung’ is unnecessary in established POV.
decisions.replacement: But he could not contain his curiosity. How would that bastard grow? How far would he climb?

decisions.reason: Keeps 돌아가야 as return and 입을 열었다 as opening his mouth; SOL drops both.
‘Light up’ is the natural collocation for 환하게 밝아지는.
훈련 강도 has no possessor; ‘the training’ avoids BASE’s ambiguous ‘his.’
The absolute clause on bloodshot eyes is cleaner than stacking ‘with’ onto the stamp.
Keeps 해방됐지만, 전혀 기쁘지 않았다, and 쌓여; SOL drops the release and invents a mountain of work.
‘Behind my back’ is closer to 나 몰래 than ‘when I’m not looking.’
Preserves 그나마 as ‘at least’ and the 끝이 보인다 image BASE flattens into ‘only comfort.’
Keeps 채…기도 전에 as ‘even faded’ and 건장한 as sturdily built, not ‘burly.’
‘Onto’ versus ‘on’ is interchangeable; no improvement.
‘Singled out’ captures 지목당한 among the two servants more naturally than ‘pointed to.’
Need 단둘이 as the two of them and 근엄한 as solemn, not SOL’s ‘dignified.’
decisions.replacement: Once the two of them were alone, Jin Wikyung began speaking in a solemn voice.

decisions.reason: ‘Been finding’ fits ongoing 요즘 better than SOL’s one-time ‘have you found.’
할 만 is ‘very well,’ and 은덕 is kindness, not SOL’s stiff ‘agreeable’ and ‘generosity.’
The period after ‘goodness’ matches the 어이구 beat before the denial.
고개만 끄덕거렸다 is only nodding; SOL’s ‘over and over’ drops the 만.
대단하신 분 is ‘great man,’ closer than ‘esteemed person.’
혹시라도 is ‘perhaps,’ not ‘somehow.’
Keeps 차고 and 휘날리는 as paired actions; SOL’s absolute clause drops him fluttering the headband.
‘Glaze over’ is the idiom for 몽롱하게 풀어지는.
뭐야, 이놈 is ‘What’s with this guy,’ not BASE’s stronger ‘what the hell is wrong.’
SOL’s eyes ‘burned’ and ‘very soul’ intensify a look the Korean only describes as longing.
눈빛 is a look, not ‘eyes,’ and ‘give another’ is natural for 보낼 만한.
설마? is interrogative; the question mark should stay.
말로만 듣던 needs no added name or ‘ever’; SOL is wordier without gain.
식솔 is household, and 금물 is ‘must not,’ tighter than BASE’s ‘could not’ and ‘Jin Family.’
애써 지우며 is forcibly erasing suspicion, not merely setting it aside.
많이 is ‘a lot’; ‘a great deal’ is ceremonial churn.
눈여겨보다 is keeping an eye on someone, not the more predatory ‘had my eye on you.’
The 아니라…부터다 contrast reads more cleanly as one ‘not…but’ sentence.
Reliable and trustworthy are interchangeable for 믿을 만한.
였지 is past ‘that was you,’ not present ‘that’s you.’
BASE drops 일자무식; SOL restores it as ‘uneducated,’ weakens 전율했다, and italicizes the word.
decisions.replacement: Childeuk, an exceptional servant possessing all four virtues, shuddered with emotion. Completely illiterate, he had no idea what those four virtues meant, but he understood the word “talented” perfectly.

decisions.reason: ‘Being strong and diligent’ and ‘none other than’ match 힘 좋고 성실하다 and 다른 사람도 아니고.
Keeps 휩싸였다 and 혀도; SOL drops ‘even’ and the swept-up image.
움찔 몸을 떨었다 is a flinch; ‘his body flinched’ is body-part translationese.
오랫동안 is ‘a long time,’ not ‘years,’ and 언젠가 is not ‘finally.’
헛 is a startled gasp; the exclamation mark fits better than a flat ‘Ah.’
숨을 삼켰다 is swallowing a breath, not the saliva ‘swallowed’ that appears later.
그것도 이상해 is ‘that’s strange too,’ without the 말 of the previous line.
멈추지 않았다 is ‘did not stop,’ not the passive ‘could no longer be stopped.’
Keeps 이 한 몸; SOL drops ‘one’ and adds an explicit ‘you’ that spikes the sexual reading.
하지 마 and 바치지 마 are two commands; SOL collapses the first to ‘Don’t!’
가쁜 숨을 내쉬었고 is panting, more precise than ‘breathed heavily.’
‘Never imagined’ is the natural collocation for 생길 줄이야.
아무리…라고 해도 is ‘no matter how,’ stronger than SOL’s ‘though.’
되는 is ‘become’ the object, tighter than ‘be the object of them.’
Restores 가슴이 쿵쾅거렸다, which BASE omits.
시켜만 주십시오 is ‘just give the order,’ closer than ‘tell me to do it.’
SOL’s split is more readable, but ‘tremendous force’ oversells 강력했다 and ‘crumpled’ drifts from 쓰러진.
decisions.replacement: A slap from a Peak master was powerful. Childeuk collapsed like a puppet with its strings cut. Jin Wikyung stared down at him, breathing hard, then hurriedly rang the bell.

decisions.reason: 헉 is a gasp of shock; ‘Gasp!’ beats a period.
Both soften 끌고 나가게 to ‘take’; the order is to drag him out.
The period after ‘No’ matches 아닐세 as a cutoff before 됐네.
식솔 is household, but SOL’s ‘rage’ and ‘mixture’ intensify 분노와 서러움.
decisions.replacement: He could not possibly say such a thing to a member of his household. For the first time in his life, anger and wounded sorrow brought him close to tears.

decisions.reason: 덧붙였다 is adding the line, not merely remembering it.
주어진 is ‘given,’ and ‘possessing’ is less awkward than ‘possessor of.’
‘Don’t let him anywhere near’ is tighter spoken English for 얼씬거리지 못하게.
위해서다 is purpose, not SOL’s ‘I don’t want,’ but BASE’s ‘would not/learned’ is too stiff for the diary.
decisions.replacement: So I won’t forget what I learn during this training.

decisions.reason: The 는데 link is ‘and’; splitting is merely different.
죽어라 is manner of swinging, not SOL’s result ‘until I nearly died’; ‘Maybe that’s why’ is better diary voice for 그 덕분인지.
decisions.replacement: I swung my spear to the point of death again today. Maybe that’s why my Strength and Stamina stats increased, and the Jin Family’s Spear Technique reached the ninth stage.

decisions.reason: Diary-natural ‘I’m progressing’ and ‘spending this time learning’ match 이 시간에 익히는.
‘Is getting’ is more current diary voice for 귀찮아졌다 than ‘has become.’
정신이 썩어 빠졌단다 is a rotten mind, not attitude.
Fronting the sleep complaint is more natural English for the same 이래 clause.
SOL’s cycle list matches 반복, but ‘living on’ and ‘takes too long’ drift from 시간도 아깝다고 때우기.
decisions.replacement: Most of my time is spent repeating the same cycle with Jin Mukyung: training, sparring, training, sparring. Starting yesterday, I began using fasting pills instead of wasting time eating.

decisions.reason: 슬슬 is ‘starting to’ reach the limit.
열받아서 is ‘pissed off,’ matching the diary’s register better than ‘angry.’
하나 올랐다 is increased by one; SOL drops the quantity.
지긋지긋하게 is relentless grinding, and ‘just walking around’ is more spoken than ‘simply.’
내가 알던 무공이 아닌 is not the arts he knew; BASE reverses the polarity.
The Day 9 punchline is terse diary ‘get it,’ not the flatter ‘understand.’
보며 is looking at the sword, not looking down; SOL adds an unsupported ‘down.’
아슬아슬하게 성공이군 comments on the success, not ‘you barely managed it.’
멍하니 is blankly, fitting the realization; ‘in a daze’ suggests stunned confusion.
이런 거였구나 is ‘this,’ pointing at the present moment.
SOL’s tense is cleaner, but ‘reached the middle’ misbinds 올랐다고, which belongs to the false summit.
decisions.replacement: I had thought I knew the martial arts I’d learned inside and out. But I was wrong. I had merely mistaken the middle of the mountain for the summit.

decisions.reason: ‘Whenever’ and ‘every time’ both cover 때마다; no real gain.
